brief: CIB-related index rebalancing around last Friday's quad-witching distorted headline US equity ETF flow prints, making them unusually noisy. Adjusting for estimated CIB effects, US equity inflows were modestly below average, with a sector rotation out of Financials and Health Care into Tech, Communication Services, Discretionary and Industrials. International flows were weak, led by outflows from India, Korea and Japan. Fixed Income and Commodity ETFs posted strong inflows while Currency/Multi-asset ETFs were near-average. In rates, ETF investors and Asset Managers cut duration. In commodities, Managed Money sharply reduced Copper longs week over week, while Energy ETF inflows skewed toward inverse oil products. In futures, large net buying hit MID, CAC 40, JSE Top 40, ASX 200, UK 10-year, GBP, JPY, CAD and CHF, while large net selling hit BIST 30, China A50 and CSI 300. CTAs likely remain net long global equities and added to longs, stayed broadly short global rates outside China, likely bought copper, remain long Energy and Agriculture, and hold mixed FX exposure versus the dollar.
